lock: Five pins are cut in two and block the cylinder. Only your key lifts every cut to the same line, so nothing is in the way and it turns.
jack: A small piston pushes oil under a much bigger one. The same pressure on ten times the area gives ten times the force, and a valve stops the oil flowing back.
speaker: Current turns a coil of wire into a magnet, and the fixed magnet around it pushes and pulls it thousands of times a second. The cone moves the air. That is sound.
seatbelt: Pull slowly and the spool turns freely. Yank it, or stop the car hard, and a small weight moves and drops a catch into a ring of teeth.
door: The latch bolt has one slanted side. The strike plate pushes on the slant, the bolt slides in, and a spring snaps it back out once it reaches the hole.
windows: Stress in the cabin's skin flows around each window. At a sharp corner it piles up and a crack can start, so every window, door and hatch is rounded.
windows2: Stress in the cabin's skin flows around each window. At a sharp corner it piles up and a crack can start, so every window, door and hatch is rounded.
bike: Spring-loaded pawls in the hub bite into slanted teeth when you pedal. When you coast, the teeth slide past and each pawl snaps back down. That is the click.
elevator: A governor wheel senses the speed. Too fast, and it trips steel wedges that clamp the guide rails. The harder the car pulls, the harder they grip.
combo: Behind the dial sit three wheels, each with one notch. Every number parks one notch at the top. When all three line up, a bar drops in and frees the shackle.
clock: An anchor holds the gears back and lets them slip one tooth for each swing of the pendulum. Every catch is a tick, and every slip gives the pendulum a tiny push.
zipper: Each tooth has a bump on top and a hollow underneath. The slider is a wedge that feeds the two rows together at an angle, so every bump drops into the next hollow.
pen: Each click pushes a toothed cam past ribs in the barrel and turns it one notch. It rests on a high ledge one time (tip out) and drops into a deep slot the next (tip in).
kettle: Steam reaches a small disc made of two metals. One stretches more with heat, so the disc snaps inside out and flicks the switch off.
sprinkler: A glass bulb of liquid holds a plug against the water. Heat makes the liquid expand until the glass shatters. Only the sprinklers above the fire open.
tape: The hook slides by exactly its own thickness. Hooked over an edge, zero is its inside face. Pushed against a wall, zero is its outside face.
musicbox: Pins on a turning cylinder pluck the teeth of a steel comb. Long teeth ring low, short teeth ring high. The song is written in pins.
switch: You squeeze a spring until the lever passes its centre. Then the spring flips the contacts together in a blink, too fast for a spark to burn them.
escalator: Each step rides on two pairs of wheels on two tracks. On the slope the tracks keep every step level. At the landing they come together and the steps form a flat floor.
valve: A spring holds a rubber seal on its seat, and the air in the tyre pushes it the same way. More pressure means a tighter seal. Pressing the pin lifts it.
stapler: A blade pushes one staple through the paper onto a plate with two curved grooves. The staple never folds itself. The grooves fold it.
pencil: Three jaws grip the lead. A click slides jaws and lead forward together, a stop opens the jaws, and they slide back alone to grab the lead further up.
can: First the tab pivots on its nose and cracks a vent to let the gas out. Then the rivet becomes the pivot and the nose pushes the lid in. One tab, two levers.
nozzle: Fuel rushing through the handle sucks air in through a small hole at the tip. When the fuel covers the hole, the suction jumps and unlatches the trigger.
trainwheels: Each wheel is a cone on a solid axle. In a curve the pair shifts outward, so the outer wheel rolls on its wide part and travels farther. The train steers itself.
lighter: A spring presses a soft metal rod against a steel wheel. Spinning the wheel shaves off specks that burn white hot, just as a lever opens the gas.
ballpoint: A tiny ball sits in a socket and rolls ink from behind onto the page. Land the pen on its tip and the socket dents. The ball jams, so no ink.
coincheck: A gauge checks the size and a magnet holds steel slugs. The same magnet slows real coins by an amount that depends on the metal, and only the right speed reaches the cash box.
sawbrake: The blade carries a small electric signal that skin changes and wood does not. Within a few thousandths of a second a spring fires a metal block into the teeth.
sewing: The needle's eye is at its tip, so it pushes a loop of thread under the cloth. A hook carries that loop around a second spool below, and the two threads lock.
points: Two tapered blades, tied together, slide sideways. One closes against its rail and guides the wheel by its flange. The other opens a gap for the opposite wheel.
teapot: A wall splits the pot in two, and each side has its own air hole. Liquid can only leave if air gets in behind it, so plugging a hole holds that drink back.
glowstick: A thin glass vial inside the tube. When it breaks, two liquids mix and react. The reaction hands its energy to a dye, and the dye gives it back as light.
starter: An electromagnet pulls a lever that slides a small gear into the teeth of the flywheel. Only then does the motor get full power. Let go, and a spring pulls the gear back.
greedycup: The centre column hides a bent tube. Fill past the bend and the tube becomes a siphon that drains the whole cup through the base.
engine: Four strokes, over and over. The piston sucks in air and fuel, squeezes them, a spark sets them off and the blast drives it down, then it pushes the exhaust out.
coupler: Each car ends in a hinged steel knuckle. When two cars bump, the knuckles swing shut around each other and a heavy lock drops behind each one, so it cannot swing open again.
differential: The axle is split in two, and small gears in a spinning cage join the halves. Driving straight they ride along; in a turn they roll, so one wheel speeds up exactly as much as the other slows.
stylus: A record has one long groove whose walls waver in the shape of the sound. A tiny diamond follows the waver and shakes a magnet beside a coil, which turns the motion into an electric signal.
ratchet: Inside the head, a spring-loaded catch presses against a toothed wheel. Pulling one way, the catch jams on a tooth and turns the bolt; swinging back, it rides up each slope and clicks over.
torquewrench: A spring in the handle presses a small block square into a notch. When your pull reaches the set force the block tips over with a click. It only warns you: the wrench still turns the nut.
doorcloser: Opening the door pushes a piston against a spring. The spring pushes back, but the oil ahead of the piston can only escape through one tiny hole, so the door closes slowly.
